newsitem.title: USA: Fed could stay out of market, coupon pass possible.
newsitem.headline: Fed could stay out of market, coupon pass possible.

text.p: The Federal Reserve could refrain from open market operations on Friday, with Federal funds trading at a soft 5-1/8 percent, analysts said.

The "window of opportunity" for the Fed to add permanent reserves to the banking system by buying coupons was open, analysts said, though opinion was divided about whether the coupon pass would be down before the Thanksgiving holiday next week or after it.
"We're looking for nothing today, but the window for a possible coupon pass starts today," said James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc.
Glassman said the overnight system repurchases that the Fed conducted on Thursday led many people to think that the coupon pass would take place sooner, rather than later.

"The reserve need isn't quite as large as I used to think but there is a need for reserves," said Glassman. "That need could be addressed with a series of term RPs, but the custom (this season) is to address it outright with a coupon pass."
Patrick Dimick, trader and Treasury market strategist at UBS Securities, said he thought it more likely that the Fed would buy coupons during the first week of December.
"They could start today, do two legs, then another leg on Monday and a fourth leg on Tuesday," said Dimick. "It's likely they'd start today if they do it before December."
But Dimick said there's no pattern to the Fed's method of buying coupons.
"They've done all sectors of the yield curve in one day or over several days," he said. "There's no detectable pattern and I think that's intentional."

Analysts at MMS International said they expected the Fed to intervene with term system repurchases, even though Federal funds are trading at a soft 5-1/8 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
"A coupon pass is still in the cards," the MMS analysts said, "but the timing is uncertain."
